hook: The emperor who ruled half of Europe and the Americas, then gave it all up.

pages.x: Charles was born in Ghent in 1500. From his four grandparents he inherited the Netherlands, Spain with its new American empire, southern Italy, and the Habsburg lands in Austria. In 1519 he was elected Holy Roman Emperor as well. He was 19.
He had the famous Habsburg jaw, so jutting that he could hardly close his mouth or chew. A peasant once called out to him: "Majesty, shut your mouth! The flies of this country are very rude."

pages.t: The empire where the sun never set
pages.x: In his reign Cortés conquered Mexico, Pizarro conquered Peru, and Magellan's fleet sailed around the world in his name. His lands circled the globe, and people said the sun never set on them.
He fought France for Italy and captured its king at Pavia in 1525. He fought the Ottomans from Vienna to Tunis. His unpaid troops sacked Rome in 1527 and held the pope prisoner.
In 1521 at Worms he faced Martin Luther and made him an outlaw. He spent decades trying to stop the Reformation, but in 1555 he had to accept that each German prince could choose his own faith.

Worn out by gout and endless war, he did something almost no monarch had done: in 1556 he gave up his crowns, Spain to his son Philip and the empire to his brother Ferdinand, and retired to a monastery at Yuste in Spain.

At Yuste he collected clocks and tried in vain to make them all tick together. He is said to have remarked that if he could not make two clocks agree, he had been foolish to think he could make men agree. He died in 1558.

Charles V ruled the largest empire Europe had seen since Charlemagne, the first on which the sun never set. He could not stop the Reformation, but he made the Habsburgs the most powerful family in Europe for two centuries.
pts: Ruled Spain, the Netherlands and the Holy Roman Empire
Reigned over the first worldwide empire
